record.original_question: If D is restricted to be an orientation of a cubic graph, can the arcs of D be partitioned into two linear forests?

evidence.quote: What about if D is the orientation of a cubic graph

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D$ be a directed graph (digraph). A directed linear forest in $D$ is a set of arcs forming a vertex-disjoint union of directed paths; equivalently, a subdigraph in which every vertex has in-degree at most $1$ and out-degree at most $1$, and whose underlying undirected graph is acyclic. A cubic graph is a $3$-regular simple graph, and an orientation of a cubic graph $G$ is a digraph $D$ obtained from $G$ by assigning a direction to each edge.

Question: Is it true that for every orientation $D$ of every cubic graph $G$, the arc set of $D$ can be partitioned into two directed linear forests?
artifact.status_search_result: The closely related Nakayama–Péroche conjecture states that every digraph with maximum in- and out-degree $\Delta$ has dilinear arboricity at most $\Delta+1$, which for orientations of cubic graphs would give at most $4$. The undirected analogue (linear arboricity $2$ for cubic graphs) is a classical theorem, but a definitive published result establishing or refuting the $2$-linear-forest partition for every orientation of every cubic graph was not located in the searches. Status appears unresolved in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Linear arboricity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: For cubic graphs and other graphs of maximum degree three, the linear arboricity is always two.
status_evidence.claim: The undirected linear arboricity of every cubic graph is 2, but this is the undirected statement and does not directly resolve the digraph version.

status_evidence.title: The linear k-arboricity of digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: A directed linear forest is a disjoint union of directed paths; the linear arboricity of a digraph was introduced by Nakayama and Péroche.
status_evidence.claim: The directed analogue is studied via the Nakayama–Péroche framework; specific results for orientations of cubic graphs were not located.

status_evidence.title: The List Linear Arboricity of Digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies linear arboricity bounds for digraphs in terms of maximum semi-degree.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit confirmation that two directed linear forests suffice for every orientation of a cubic graph was found.
